newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.03 pct in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.03 pct in volatile trade.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.03 percent in volatile trade to close at 1.0720 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank lowered the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank fulfilled market expectations Thursday by depreciating the mini-band for the first time this month, lowering it 0.09 percent to between 1.0710 and 1.0760 reais per dollar.
Analysts said the real dropped less than the mini-band allowed because the market had already traded close to the new limit on Wednesday, when the local currency closed at 1.0717 per greenback.

The real was traded between 1.0715 and 1.0732 per dollar throughout the day, with players following the direction of dollar flows. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts at 1645 local/1945 GMT showed a $110 million deficit.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.04 percent to end at 1.0760 per greenback.
In the parallel market, the real closed flat at 1.132 per dollar, traders said.
